thread:
matt: heads-up — I ran the funcall holdout suite against sanitywave-int8 on the small holdout (funcall-holdout-2026-02). baseline (fp16) pass rate 98.6%, sanitywave-int8 is at 93.2% so we have a regression to dig into.

sara: ouch. where are the failures concentrated? structured or nonjson suffixes?

matt: 70% of failures are strict-schema rejects (missing keys / trailing commas), 20% are non-JSON suffixes, 10% are weird valid-json but wrong types (string vs array).

jia: can you paste an example of the typical malformed one? small snippet is fine.

matt: sure — example from the canary: 

```json
{"action": "create_ticket", "params": {"title": "Login bug",}, "confidence": 0.92}
```

note the trailing comma after "title". fp16 rarely produced that.

sara: that smells like tokenizer/quant rounding pushing an extra token before closing brace. do we see it more in streaming mode?

matt: yes — streaming outputs have a 3x higher trailing-comma rate for this model. non-streaming still has a small bump vs fp16.

omar: interesting. what about KV prefix caching? does the holdout include starts with a long system prefix?

matt: holdout has a ~240-token prompt prefix for context. I re-ran with prefix_cache disabled: trailing-comma failures dropped by ~40%.

jia: ok that's a lead. maybe caching + int8 rounding interacts with beam of next-token probs. we should run A/B canary with two configs: (A) prefix_cache on, retry.max_attempts=2, (B) prefix_cache off, retry.max_attempts=1. measure schema-pass per 1k calls and median latency.

sara: agree. also let's add a parser-rescue step in the client to try a quick post-hoc repair before marking as failure: 1) strip trailing commas, 2) try NDJSON split, 3) wrap in array if top-level missing. cheap heuristic only — track how often it changes semantics.

matt: plan: I'll spin up two canaries (A/B) in staging with 5k calls each. script below used for the runs: 

```bash
for cfg in A B; do
  curl -s -X POST "https://staging.redwood.dev/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGE_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"sanitywave-int8","input":"$PROMPT","stream":'$( [ "$cfg" = A ] && echo true || echo false ),"prefix_cache":'$( [ "$cfg" = A ] && echo true || echo false ),"retry":{"max_attempts":'$( [ "$cfg" = A ] && echo 2 || echo 1 )}}' \
    >> results_$cfg.jsonl
  sleep 0.05
done
```

(just a toy example, will run via our runner)

omar: can you add a small eval step after collection to compute: schema_pass_rate, posthoc_repair_rate, repaired_consistency_rate (how often repairs change the intended action), median_latency.

matt: yes — runner will produce that. expected metrics: baseline fp16 schema_pass_rate=0.986, sanitywave-int8(A) schema_pass_rate ~0.932, sanitywave-int8(B) maybe 0.956 if prefix_cache off helps.

jia: also add a quick token-entropy diagnostic on the failing examples to see if distribution is peaky or flat. quantization sometimes makes local distribution flatter and increases chance of odd tokens.

sara: good call. if entropy for fails is higher than normal, we can justify more aggressive retry or soft-schema with suggested corrections.

eval-bot: new run scheduled by matt — job id rw-canary-3265. will post artifacts here when done. ETA ~ 40m.

matt: thanks — I'll also attach raw samples and a small PR for the client heuristic. if canary shows B wins without latency regression, we can ship prefix_cache:false for int8 models as a temporary mitigation.

omar: FYI, let's not change global defaults yet. prefer model-tagged override in routing table + a flag in model metadata (avoid surprising dedicated customers).

sara: +1. also create an entry in the onboarding checklist to run this holdout and record schema_pass_rate delta >= 1% as a blocker.

jia: added to checklist draft. once canary artifacts are posted I can run the statistical test and write up short triage.

matt: perfect — will ping when rw-canary-3265 finishes. :thumbsup:
